packet.description_seed: The Russian leader sees potential for Ukraine negotiations, but condemns the West's backing for President Zelensky.

what: Putin says he thinks Ukraine conflict 'coming to an end'

clean_source_blocks.text: The Russian leader sees potential for Ukraine negotiations, but condemns the West's backing for President Zelensky.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has said he thinks Russia's conflict with Ukraine is coming to an end, addressing reporters after a scaled-back military parade in Moscow marking the Soviet victory in World War Two. "I think that the matter is coming to an end," he said, referring to the "special military operation" in Ukraine, while condemning Western support for the Kyiv government. Russia's annual parade lacked the usual display of tanks and missiles, due to security concerns as authorities feared Ukraine might target Red Square with drones. A last-minute ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv, brokered by US President Donald Trump, reduced the danger of any attack and the parade passed off without incident. Putin's comments came just hours after he used his Victory Parade speech to justify the war.

Russian President Vladimir Putin suggested the war in Ukraine was drawing to a close — just hours after he vowed to triumph at Moscow’s puniest Victory Day parade in years. “I think that the matter is coming to an end,” Putin told reporters inside the Kremlin Saturday about the four-year-long war. Putin said the United States — which he referred to as a “partner” and “friend” during his remarks, alongside the likes of China and India — was eager to help broker a deal. “Clearly, they have no need for this conflict, as they have many other priorities,” he said. “But this is, first and foremost, a matter for Russia and Ukraine.”

In that speech he said Russia was fighting a "just" war and called Ukraine an "aggressive force" that was being "armed and supported by the whole bloc of Nato". Later, when asked at a news conference about the West helping Ukraine, Putin said: "They (West) promised assistance and then began fuelling a confrontation with Russia that continues to this day. I think that the matter is coming to an end, but it is a serious matter." Putin also said he would only meet Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky once a lasting peace deal was agreed to. "A meeting in a third country is also possible, but only once final agreements have been reached on a peace treaty for a long‑term historical perspective, to take part in this event and sign (treaty), but it must be a final step," he continued.

[Lähde: New York Post]
Russian President Vladimir Putin suggested the war in Ukraine was drawing to a close — just hours after he vowed to triumph at Moscow’s puniest Victory Day parade in years.

“I think that the matter is coming to an end,” Putin told reporters inside the Kremlin Saturday about the four-year-long war.

Putin said the United States — which he referred to as a “partner” and “friend” during his remarks, alongside the likes of China and India — was eager to help broker a deal.

“Clearly, they have no need for this conflict, as they have many other priorities,” he said.

“But this is, first and foremost, a matter for Russia and Ukraine.”

The strongman said he would be willing to sit-down with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in a neutral country, but only once final agreements to end the war have been reached.

“This must be the final step, not some negotiations,” Putin said, according to state-run TASS news agency.

“I have never refused” to meet Zelensky, he claimed. “I am not proposing this meeting, but if someone proposes it, then let them come. Whoever wants to meet should come to Moscow, and we will meet.”

He lashed out at “globalist” Western leaders, saying they pledged after the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 that NATO would not expand eastward — only to later pull Ukraine toward their orbit.

His remarks come on the heels of a fragile three-day cease-fire between the warring countries brokered by Washington to coincide with Russia’s annual Victory Day parade, marking the Soviet Union’s historic victory over Nazi Germany in World War II.

“Hopefully, it is the beginning of the end of a very long, deadly, and hard fought War,” President Trump posted on Truth Social.

Trump said he was ready to send a high-powered US delegation into Moscow as part of an intensified push to end the deadly conflict, with talks stalled since the start of the war in Iran on Feb. 28.

“I would very much like to see the end of the conflict,” Trump told reporters during a press gaggle near the White House Saturday.

The two sides are still far apart when it comes to a deal though, with the main obstacle over who will get control of the contested Donbas region.

payload.title: Putin väittää Ukrainan sodan olevan lähestymässä loppuaan
payload.summary: Venäjän presidentti Vladimir Putin sanoo uskovansa, että Ukrainan sota on etenemässä kohti ratkaisua, mutta syyttää samalla länttä konfliktin pitkittämisestä tukemalla Kiovaa.
payload.content:
Venäjän presidentti Vladimir Putin on sanonut uskovansa, että Venäjän sota Ukrainassa on ”lähestymässä loppuaan”. Hän esitti arvionsa toimittajille Moskovassa voitonpäivän sotilasparaatin jälkeen ja arvosteli samalla länsimaiden tukea Ukrainan presidentti Volodymyr Zelenskyin hallinnolle.

## Kommentit supistetun paraatin jälkeen

Putin puhui toimittajille sen jälkeen, kun Venäjä oli järjestänyt vuosittaisen voitonpäivän paraatinsa toisen maailmansodan neuvostovoiton muistoksi. Paraati oli lähdetietojen mukaan aiempaa suppeampi, eikä siinä nähty tavanomaista tankkien ja ohjusten esittelyä.

Turvallisuushuolet vaikuttivat paraatin järjestelyihin, sillä Venäjän viranomaiset pelkäsivät Ukrainan mahdollisesti kohdistavan drooni-iskuja Punaiselle torille. Moskovan ja Kiovan välinen viime hetken tulitauko vähensi hyökkäyksen vaaraa, ja paraati sujui ilman välikohtauksia.

Putinin lausunnot tulivat vain tunteja sen jälkeen, kun hän oli käyttänyt voitonpäivän puheensa sodan oikeuttamiseen. Puheessa hän kuvasi Venäjän käyvän ”oikeutettua” sotaa ja kutsui Ukrainaa aggressiiviseksi voimaksi, jota hänen mukaansa aseistaa ja tukee koko Nato-blokki.

## Yhdysvallat ja mahdollinen sovittelu

Putin viittasi myös Yhdysvaltoihin, jonka hän kuvasi puheissaan halukkaaksi auttamaan sovun välittämisessä. Hänen mukaansa Yhdysvalloilla ei ole tarvetta konfliktille, koska sillä on muita painopisteitä. Samalla Putin korosti, että kyse on ennen kaikkea Venäjän ja Ukrainan välisestä asiasta.

Kun Putinilta kysyttiin lännen Ukrainalle antamasta avusta, hän syytti länttä vastakkainasettelun ruokkimisesta Venäjän kanssa. Hänen mukaansa länsi oli ensin luvannut apua Ukrainalle ja alkanut sen jälkeen ylläpitää konfliktia, joka jatkuu edelleen.

## Zelenskyi-tapaaminen vasta sopimuksen lopuksi

Putin sanoi olevansa valmis tapaamaan Ukrainan presidentin Volodymyr Zelenskyin vasta siinä vaiheessa, kun pitkäaikaisesta rauhansopimuksesta olisi päästy lopulliseen yhteisymmärrykseen. Hänen mukaansa tapaaminen kolmannessa maassa voisi olla mahdollinen, mutta vain sopimuksen allekirjoittamisen viimeisenä vaiheena.

Lausunnot eivät tarkoita, että neuvotteluissa olisi lähdetietojen perusteella tapahtunut konkreettinen läpimurto. Putinin arvio sodan päättymisestä on hänen oma poliittinen tulkintansa, joka esitettiin samaan aikaan, kun Venäjä jatkoi sodan perustelua ja arvosteli voimakkaasti lännen tukea Ukrainalle.
